svg.title: Session 02 setup, step by step
svg.desc: Animated walkthrough: four Lima VMs, the jumpbox downloading and sorting binaries, machines.txt, root SSH, hostnames, and the restart problem and fix.
svg.text: Your Mac · Lima VMs on the user-v2 network

g.text: client/ · kubectl
controller/ → server
worker/ → nodes
cni-plugins/ → nodes
machines.txt
id_rsa · SSH key

svg.text: No pod subnet (no pods run here)

g.text: 1 · Four VMs
Lima boots four Debian 12 VMs on your Mac, each with its own Linux kernel, on one virtual
network (192.168.104.x). The ping test proved they can reach each other.
2 · Download the binaries
The jumpbox downloads 11 binaries: the six Kubernetes components (v1.32.3) plus etcd,
containerd, runc, the CNI plugins and crictl from other projects. Each Kubernetes component is
a single file.
3 · Sort by role
The binaries are sorted into folders by where they'll run: controller/ is headed for the
server, worker/ and cni-plugins/ for the two nodes. Nothing has been copied to those machines
yet.
4 · machines.txt
A one-line-per-machine inventory: IP, full name, short name and pod subnet. Each node gets its
own range of pod addresses, separate from the VMs' real IPs. The server gets none because no
pods run there.
5 · Root SSH from the jumpbox
The jumpbox generates a key pair. Its public half goes into root's authorized_keys on each
machine (via limactl, since there's no root password). Now the jumpbox can run commands as root
anywhere, which every later lab relies on.
6 · Names
Each machine gets its real hostname and a full name ending in .kubernetes.local. One shared
hosts file goes to every machine, so they all find each other by name. Certificates in Session
03 will list these names.
7 · Restart: what broke
Lima gives a VM a new cloud-init instance ID on every start. cloud-init thinks it's a brand-new
machine: it resets the hostname and regenerates the SSH host key. The jumpbox sees a different
identity and refuses: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED.
8 · The fix
A cloud-init setting on each machine (preserve_hostname: true, ssh_deletekeys: false) keeps the
hostname and host key across restarts. Verified by restarting node-1: same name, same IP, same
key.
Next · Session 03
The jumpbox becomes the certificate authority. It will sign a certificate for each component,
naming it by the hostnames you just set, and send each one over these SSH links. The SSH
warning in step 7 is the same identity problem TLS solves.
